boundary: This registry predicts TOOL SELECTION against a mock MCP that returns deterministic stubs. It says nothing about whether the real tool then produces a correct answer (epic 1) and nothing about end-to-end performance versus grep (discovery epic).

variant_meaning.a: live verbatim (the shipped LCI descriptions) - the baseline every delta is taken against
variant_meaning.b: task-framed ('Use when you need ...'), same facts, no neighbor contrast
variant_meaning.c: example-augmented (baseline text plus one example invocation)
variant_meaning.d: disambiguated (baseline text plus an explicit 'Unlike <neighbor>, ...' contrast)

grid.models_verified: `opencode models` (opencode 1.18.26, 2026-09-06) lists both ids; both are free-tier. No paid provider is used.
grid.reps_note: Reps are separate ledgers. If 3 x 128 live cells is not reachable in wall-clock on the free fleet, reps are reduced and the reduction is stated in the analysis; tasks and variants are never reduced.

decision_rule.unit: correct-first-call rate = correct_first_call / denominator, per (variant, model, tier); non-selection outcomes (provider_*, exit_*, no_tool_call, hallucinated_tool, empty_answer) are excluded from the denominator and reported separately.
decision_rule.spread: run-to-run spread for a cell = max(rate) - min(rate) across reps of variant A in the same (model, tier) stratum.
decision_rule.lift: A variant is credited with a lift over A only if BOTH hold: (1) mean(rate_variant) - mean(rate_A) > spread_A, and (2) neighbor precision does not fall: the rate at which the tool is wrongly called first on the OTHER tasks that name it as a confusable neighbor does not rise by more than spread_A.
decision_rule.regression_flag: A recall gain that arrives with a neighbor-precision loss is reported as a REGRESSION, never as a win.
decision_rule.null: A gap that does not exceed the run-to-run spread is reported as no effect, not as a small lift.

global_predictions.claim: Variant D reduces the search<->callers confusion seen in the E2.3 smoke: on task confirmed-call-sites-for-one-routine the first-call column `search` drops to zero under D, and on task where-does-this-text-appear the column `callers` does not rise.
global_predictions.falsified_if: D still shows any `search` first call on the callers task, or D raises `callers` first calls on the search task above spread.

global_predictions.claim: The weak tier gains more from the best variant than the strong tier does, mirroring the output epic's weak-tier-gains-most result: (best_variant - A) on weak exceeds (best_variant - A) on strong by at least one task's worth of rate.
global_predictions.falsified_if: The strong tier's gain equals or exceeds the weak tier's, or the weak tier's gain does not exceed spread at all.

global_predictions.claim: The control task control-corpus-readiness shows NO variant effect: every variant selects index_stats at the same rate within spread, on both models.
global_predictions.falsified_if: Any variant moves the control task's correct rate by more than spread. That would mean the instrument responds to wording where no ambiguity exists, and every other delta becomes suspect.

global_predictions.claim: native:* first calls (the strong model opening with bash/read, seen in every E2.3 strong cell) are the dominant non-correct column on the strong tier and do NOT fall under any variant: description wording cannot compete with a built-in tool the model already trusts.
global_predictions.falsified_if: Any variant lowers the strong tier's native:* column by more than spread.

global_predictions.claim: Variant C (example invocations) does not lift selection over A beyond spread on either tier: an example teaches ARGUMENT shape, not which tool to reach for.
global_predictions.falsified_if: C beats A by more than spread on either tier.

global_predictions.claim: hallucinated:* first calls stay under 5% of attempted cells on both tiers and are not moved by variant.
global_predictions.falsified_if: Any (variant, model) cell exceeds 5% hallucinated first calls.
